ideas.title: Stop applying, start messaging
ideas.hook: Only 2 to 3 percent of job applications turn into interviews. So I stopped applying.
ideas.why: Recruiters now lean on AI filters (LinkedIn's Hiring Assistant), so a direct message beats one more application. VICE cites a 2–3% interview rate for applications.
ideas.script:
[Talking to camera, phone in hand]
Only 2 to 3 percent of job applications turn into interviews. So I stopped applying. Well — I stopped ONLY applying.
Now for every job I actually want, I message someone on the team. The problem is cold messages sound cold. "Hi, I'm interested in the role" gets left on read.
[Screen recording: LinkedIn profile open, LinkedAI panel]
So I've been using this extension called LinkedAI. You open someone's profile and it finds real common ground between you two — same school, same old company, a project you both worked on — and writes the message around that.
[Point at screen]
Look — it caught that we both interned at the same place. I would never have noticed that.
That's the difference between being ignored and getting "sure, happy to chat."
[Back to camera]
It's free on the Chrome Web Store. Link's in my bio. Go message someone today.

ideas.title: Your cover letter sounds like a robot
ideas.hook: If your cover letter starts with 'I am excited to apply,' the recruiter already knows.
ideas.why: Reviewers of Simplify+ and Jobscan keep calling their AI writing generic or keyword-stuffed, and those tools charge $40–50 a month. Tailored-from-the-actual-job-post is the gap.
ideas.script:
[Talking to camera, a bit dramatic]
If your cover letter starts with "I am excited to apply," the recruiter already knows. A chatbot wrote it — and so did the other 200 people.
The fix isn't writing it yourself at 2am. It's giving the AI the actual job post.
[Screen recording: LinkedIn job page]
I use this Chrome extension called LinkedAI. You open the job on LinkedIn, it pulls the whole posting — requirements, tools, the weird specific stuff — and builds a resume and cover letter that match THAT job. Not a template.
[Scroll the generated letter]
See how it mentions the exact tools they listed? That's what gets you past the filter and makes a human actually read it.
You can get both together as a bundle, which is cheaper than doing them one by one.
[Back to camera]
It's on the Chrome Web Store, free to try. Link in bio. Stop sending robot letters.

ideas.title: UGC brief: 'The recruiter has AI. So should you.'
ideas.hook: Recruiters are using AI to filter you out. Here's the AI I use back.
ideas.why: Sponsored creator reads like @charlottechaze's Tsenta video use the 'their AI vs. your AI' angle with a trial link. Jobright is only starting on referral outreach, so LinkedAI can own 'AI that gets you a real conversation'.
ideas.script:
WHO: Job-seeking creators (students, new grads, career switchers), 5k–100k followers, face-to-camera style.
PAY: Flat fee + affiliate commission on Pro signups via their link.
LENGTH: 30–45s, vertical, natural lighting, phone screen recording for the demo.
ANGLE: "Recruiters use AI to filter you. I use AI to skip the pile." You're a job seeker who found a useful tool — never imply you know the founder or helped build it.
STRUCTURE:
1) Hook (first 2s): the recruiter-AI line, or your own version of it.
2) The pain: applying to dozens of jobs and hearing nothing.
3) Demo 1: open a LinkedIn job → LinkedAI makes a resume + cover letter matched to that post.
4) Demo 2: open a hiring manager's profile → LinkedAI finds something you have in common and writes the message. Show the common-ground line on screen.
5) Result: what you'd send / what happened (only real results).
6) CTA: "It's free on the Chrome Web Store — my link's in bio."
MUST: Disclose as an ad (#ad or paid partnership label). Don't promise interviews or jobs. Don't name competitors or quote their prices.
AVOID: Reading a script word for word; overselling.

items.title: Simplify's founder post pitched one clear promise and got a 2,000-person waitlist
items.creator: Michael Yan / Simplify
items.whyItWorks: A single plain promise to a pain people already feel beat cold emails. LinkedAI's promise is a message that finds real common ground; lead every video with that one outcome.

items.title: 60-second green-screen job video topped 182,000 views
items.creator: Makena Yee (via The Interview Guys)
items.whyItWorks: Job-hunt videos with a face, a clear first-3-seconds claim and visual proof travel. Creators for LinkedAI should show the extension on a real profile in the first 5 seconds.

items.title: Job seekers say TikTok now beats LinkedIn for finding work; 2-3% of applications reach interviews
items.creator: VICE (Josh Katz video resume: 'hundreds of thousands of views')
items.metric: 22.1% of Gen Z use TikTok vs 20.8% LinkedIn for job search (per article)
items.whyItWorks: The audience already hangs out on TikTok and distrusts the apply button. A 'stop only applying' angle is credible there.

items.title: Free 'recruiter outreach writer' page targets 'how to message a recruiter on LinkedIn'
items.creator: Weekday
items.whyItWorks: A rival is using a free SEO tool to collect people who want to message recruiters. LinkedAI can answer the same search with a page and win on finding common ground automatically.

items.title: Teal+ sells a $13/week option reviewers call a dark pattern
items.creator: Teal (via MakerStack)
items.whyItWorks: Billing distrust is a gap. A clear monthly and yearly (20% off) Pro with no weekly trap is an easy comparison point in videos.

items.title: Simplify+ sells AI answers at $19.99/week or $39.99/month — reviewers call them generic
items.creator: Simplify (via ResumeHog review)
items.whyItWorks: The biggest free autofill tool charges ~$40/mo for AI writing people say sounds robotic. LinkedAI can win on 'sounds like you, not a bot' and a cheaper Pro.

items.title: Jobright raised its Turbo plan from $29.99 to $39.99/month; 'Insider Connections' referral feature is thin
items.creator: Jobright (via ResumeHog review)
items.whyItWorks: A big rival is moving toward referral outreach but only surfaces names. LinkedAI's common-ground messages are the step they're missing — and LinkedAI isn't US-only.

items.title: Jobscan charges $49.95/month; free plan is 5 scans and rewrites can turn keyword-stuffed
items.creator: Jobscan (via The Interview Guys)
items.whyItWorks: Job seekers between jobs feel these prices. A resume + cover letter bundle priced well under $50 is an easy comparison to make in videos and on the store listing.

items.title: LinkedIn's Hiring Assistant now plugs into ATSs like Greenhouse and Workday; LinkedIn claims 66% higher InMail acceptance
items.creator: LinkedIn (via Business Today, Sep 3 2026)
items.metric: Claimed 80% fewer profiles reviewed, +66% InMail acceptance
items.whyItWorks: Recruiters are leaning on AI to filter applicants, so cold applications matter less and direct, personal messages matter more — exactly LinkedAI's outreach pitch.

items.title: Paid creator read: 'Recruiters use AI to filter you out, so use your own AI' (Tsenta partner video)
items.creator: @charlottechaze on TikTok
items.whyItWorks: This is the exact sponsored-creator format Omar wants: an 'us vs. the recruiter's AI' hook, a free-trial link, and an 'I only partner with brands I believe in' line. A good template for LinkedAI UGC briefs.

brief.headline: Rivals charge $40–50/month for AI writing people call generic
brief.summary: Simplify+, Jobright and Jobscan all sit around $40–50 a month, and reviewers keep saying their AI resumes and letters sound robotic. Jobright is starting on referral outreach but only shows you names. Your best opening is 'AI that finds real common ground and gets you a conversation' — film the outreach script first.
filmToday: Stop applying, start messaging — Only 2 to 3 percent of job applications turn into interviews. So I stopped applying.
notes: Jobright raised its Turbo plan from $29.99 to $39.99/month and is US-only — worth targeting non-US job seekers.
LinkedIn's Hiring Assistant now connects to ATSs like Greenhouse and Workday; recruiters filtering by AI makes direct messages more valuable.
Sponsored creator reads need an #ad / paid partnership label — keep that in every creator brief.

competitors.oneLiner: Autofill Chrome extension that grew into an AI job-search copilot; job seekers of all levels.

competitors.contentStrategy: Founder-led LinkedIn posting every day as a job-search expert; best format is a job list where people comment their email.
competitors.adStrategy: Meta Ad Library and TikTok Creative Center could not be opened from this run (permission/robots block), so no ad creatives were verified. No paid-ad detail found in the articles read.
competitors.howTheyGrew: Launch post to a ~2,000 waitlist, then Squid Game-styled business cards handed out at Stanford, MIT, Berkeley, Northeastern and Harvard (sources say 10,000 to 25,000+ cards) which helped pass 10,000 users. Now claims 800K+ job seekers and 70M+ applications processed, with a team under 10.
competitors.lessonForUs: Copy the founder-free version of their best format: give something usable in seconds (a message that works) instead of explaining the product.

competitors.name: Teal
competitors.oneLiner: Resume builder, job tracker and Chrome extension for job seekers.
competitors.contentStrategy: Mostly template/SEO pages (resume examples) and review-site coverage; no verified short-video view counts found (TikTok pages blocked to this run).
competitors.adStrategy: Meta Ad Library and TikTok Creative Center could not be opened from this run (permission/robots block), so no ad creatives were verified.
competitors.howTheyGrew: Founded 2019 by Dave Fano (ex-WeWork); roughly $20M raised per MakerStack. Grew from a resume builder into a full job-search platform.
competitors.lessonForUs: Beat on billing trust: reviewers call the $13/week option a dark pattern and say cancelling is fiddly. Say 'cancel anytime' plainly.

competitors.name: Jobscan
competitors.oneLiner: Scores your resume against a job posting for ATS keywords.
competitors.price: $49.95/month or $89.95/quarter (per The Interview Guys); free plan is 5 scans
competitors.contentStrategy: Pays creators and sites through an affiliate programme rather than posting a lot itself.
competitors.adStrategy: Meta Ad Library and TikTok Creative Center could not be opened from this run (permission/robots block), so no ad creatives were verified. Jobscan runs an affiliate programme: 15% of each order, paid monthly, application and approval required, no bidding on its brand terms, no coupon sites.
competitors.lessonForUs: 15% is the benchmark for creator commission in this category. Your flat fee plus affiliate share should be at least that on Pro.

competitors.name: Careerflow
competitors.oneLiner: LinkedIn profile optimizer, job tracker and Chrome extension.
competitors.contentStrategy: Positions on LinkedIn profile optimising; claims 'well over a million users' (their claim).
competitors.adStrategy: Meta Ad Library and TikTok Creative Center could not be opened from this run (permission/robots block), so no ad creatives were verified.
competitors.howTheyGrew: Not documented in what I could read; the million-user figure is their own claim.
competitors.lessonForUs: Reviewers cite lost progress, a tight free plan and surprise renewals. Make the free plan generous and the renewal email clear.

competitors.name: AIApply
competitors.oneLiner: AI resume, cover letter, interview tools and auto-apply.
competitors.price: Premium $29/month or $144/year; Auto Apply $49/month (~100 applications); add-ons $12-19/month each
competitors.adStrategy: Meta Ad Library and TikTok Creative Center could not be opened from this run (permission/robots block), so no ad creatives were verified.
competitors.howTheyGrew: Not documented in what I could read.
competitors.lessonForUs: Total cost climbs to $49-78+/month with add-ons, and users complain it applies to poor-fit jobs and refunds are hard. Position LinkedAI as 'fewer, better messages' not bulk.

competitors.name: Weekday (free recruiter outreach writer)
competitors.oneLiner: Free no-sign-up page that drafts a cold message to a recruiter from details you type in.
channels: SEO page targeting 'how to message a recruiter on LinkedIn'
competitors.contentStrategy: A free, search-optimised tool is the top of its funnel into the job board and auto-apply.
competitors.adStrategy: Free tool as the entry point; no ads verified.
competitors.howTheyGrew: SEO tool pages feeding a job-board funnel. Its performance claims (50%+ replies, etc.) are its own, unverified.
competitors.lessonForUs: This is the closest rival to the outreach feature. It only works from what you type in; LinkedAI reads both profiles and finds common ground itself. Publish your own problem-first page for the same search.
